analysis.title: Trading Catalysts: FOMC minutes, retailers' earnings wave
key_insights: BofA economists added a January 2027 hike to their Fed forecast. They now expect 25bp hikes at the Dec, Jan and Mar meetings, taking the terminal rate to 4.50-4.75%, after hotter and broader-than-expected October inflation.
BofA says the Fed looks further behind the curve on inflation after October CPI and no longer has room to hike at a quarterly pace. It calls the risks to the new forecast balanced.
The Fed could delay or skip the last hike if data softens or financial conditions tighten significantly. A surge in wage inflation or large annual price resets could push the policy rate above 5%.

BofA expects the October FOMC minutes (Wed Nov 18, 2:00 PM ET) to show a deeper split over the decision to hold than the 10-2 vote suggested. Members favoring a hold likely argued higher yields were doing some of the Fed's work. Those opposed likely stressed economic strength and the risk of falling behind.
BofA expects subsequent data to reinforce the hawkish camp and push for a faster pace of hikes.

BofA forecasts October retail sales ex-autos and control group both +0.4% m/m, in line with consensus. BAC card spending per household rose only 0.1% m/m in October, with declines in several categories, offset partly by a rebound in online retail and supportive seasonal factors.
Holiday spending is off to a strong start, but a drop in the discretionary share of wallet in October is a concern.
The US rates team likes trading the curve with a bear flattening bias.
Market pricing shows nearly 50bp of Fed hikes over the next two meetings (Exhibit 3).

Walmart (reports Thu Nov 19 before the open): BofA expects continued share gains in grocery and general merchandise, Q3 EPS of $0.63 (roughly in line with consensus of $0.64), and full-year sales and EPS guidance at the upper end of the prior range.

Target (reports Wed Nov 18): BofA is cautious. Sales have improved, but it sees tougher comparisons, worse industry margins (freight, promotions) and limited SG&A flexibility. BofA's desk notes possible short crowding in the stock.

Home Depot (reports Tue Nov 17 before the open): BofA Q3 EPS estimate $3.83 vs consensus $3.85. Higher Pro exposure should drive outperformance. The focus shifts to supply chain costs and offsetting them as tariff refunds roll off. Share gains could support multiple expansion.

Lowe's (reports Wed Nov 18 before the open): BofA Q3 EPS estimate $2.84 vs consensus $2.90, in line with guidance for a 7% EPS decline. BofA thinks full-year guidance is derisked. Tariff refunds, not in guidance, could add about $400mn or 53c of EPS for the year.
Lowe's risks: a milder winter, since it laps a 50bp comp benefit from the winter storm in January 2025.
NVIDIA reports Tue Nov 17 after the close. Consensus EPS is $2.47 vs BofA $2.45, with a Bloomberg implied move of 8.4% against a last-8-quarter average absolute move of 4.0%.
SPX implied daily moves for the week: 0.92% Mon, 0.78% Tue, 0.91% Wed, 0.76% Thu and 0.76% Fri.
